NPCs.detail: Red was raised by his mother alone in a small house on the quiet edge of Pallet Town - a small town in the southwest of Kanto. Red struggled to make friends, with the only other children of a similar age being his neighbors, Daisy and Leaf.His mother, Delia, was very overprotective, preventing Red from leaving Pallet Town. Red yearned to leave and travel the world, becoming jealous of Leaf and all the journeys that Oak took her on. Despite his mother's protestations, the day he turned eighteen, Red applied for his trainer's license, determined to see the world that he had only heard about as a child.

Although they nominally lived in Pallet town, Oak's responsibilities took him traveling the world and he often took his granddaughters with him. Leaf grew up around exotic and unique pokemon from around the world. She grew to love all kinds of pokemon, and Oak fostered this into a passion. When she turned eighteen, she immediately applied for a trainer license, keen to follow in the footsteps of her grandfather.

When she started to fall into a bad crowd, her mother moved her to New Bark Town, hoping that some positive influences would turn her around. One day, the two of them made an idle bet on which of them could become pokemon champion first, and as the years passed they started to take it more and more seriously.

NPCs.detail: Brendan and his sister May were raised under the strict guidance of their father, Norman. As a Gym Leader, Norman ensured his children were schooled in pokemon battling from the day they could hold a pokeball. He ran them through drills, made them study historical battles, and spend every spare hour learning about pokemon battling. Brendan took to this like a Ducklett to water, embracing his father's tutelage. Norman ensured that Brendan's trainer license application was submitted the day he turned eighteen, hoping that his son would become champion of the region.

As a Gym Leader, Norman ensured his children were schooled in pokemon battling from the day they could hold a pokeball. Unlike Brendan, May rejected her father's approach to battling, instead preferring to rely on her own instincts. Despite her successes, her father and brother dismissed her victories. Despite her father's protestations, the day she turned eighteen she applied for her trainer's license, determined to show that her instincts were a superior method of battling.

NPCs.detail: Lucas grew up in Sandgem Town with a strong early interest in pokemon, driven by curiosity about how they function, behave, and interact with their environments. As a teenager, he became an assistant to Professor Rowan, quickly distinguishing himself through his analytical mindset and meticulous attention to detail. Lucas approached pokemon as subjects of study, focusing on classification, behavioral patterns, and measurable traits. Professor Rowan encouraged his structured thinking, but also pushed him to leave the laboratory and observe pokemon in the field. When Lucas turned eighteen, he applied for his trainer license, not only to strengthen his battling ability, but to expand his understanding of pokemon beyond controlled observation.

She was soon found out, but the Professor saw her potential and recruited her as his assistant, alongside Lucas. She was drawn to studying the psychological and social aspects of pokemon. When she turned eighteen, Rowan encouraged her to get her trainer's license, so she could explore the world and see research pokemon in the wild.

As he listened to these tales, he found himself filled with a desire to travel the world, a desire which quickly grew into a passion. Hilbert and Hilda convinced Cheren and Bianca to become trainers, and the four of them set out into the world together.

Watching television and movies, she saw that the greatest stars were not singers or actors, they were pokemon trainers - Gym Leaders are celebrities, important battles are widely televisied, and the pokemon league champion is more well known than any head of state. She wanted this life for herself, and so she devoted herself to becoming champion.

authorStyle: A writer of gritty, character-driven fiction with unflinching attention to the reality of pokemon.
background:
Ever since you were a child, you had a dream: To be the very best. You grew up on tales of pokemon champions, gym leaders, and elite trainers. You knew you wanted to be one of them, to have stories told about you just like the stories told about them.

The day you turned eighteen, you applied for your pokemon license, the key to becoming a trainer and realizing your dreams. You have spent months waiting, and finally you have obtained it.

Today is officially the first day of your pokemon adventure.
charSelectText:
=== IMPORTANT NOTE ===

Your choice of character determines your pool of starter pokemon, but your starting region will be chosen later.
description:
GENERATIONS 1-6 IMPLEMENTED

This is a megaworld set in the Pokemon universe. It features:
- Open world, starting in any region and challenging gyms in any order
- All 721 Pokemon from generations 1-6 obtainable, including legendaries and trade evolutions
- Expanded starter choices to all three stage evolution lines
- Robust navigation system across 321 locations
- Cross-region postgame
- 590 triggers to manage navigation, plot and progression
- 918 minor trainers, 91 major trainers and 149 special encounters
n- Heavy credit optimization, keeping turn costs below average with Smilodon and Smilodon-Thinking
descriptionRequest:
The description should be at least thirty well-written paragraphs.

When describing my location, give evocative descriptions about the landscape and the unique terrain that I pass through.

When I am fighting a pokemon battle, you must be explicit about when a battle is ongoing and when it is over. Whenever I defeat an opponent, you must explicitly state as such, using language such as `You have defeated the wild Geodude` or `You have defeated Gym Leader Misty`.
evaluationRequest:
Firstly, if I have made any assertions in my description, evaluate whether you judge that they are reasonable and likely. If they are nonsensical, incoherent or blatantly impossible, the action should be DENIED. On the other hand, if the action is trivial and there is nothing to complicate it, skip the evaluation entirely and deem the action a SUCCESS. Don't overthink this! If the action doesn't warrant further evaluation, make a judgement and move on.

Whenever pokemon are battling, the following factors should determine the winner:
- Which pokemon is higher level
- Which pokemon is has type superiority
- Which pokemon is rarer
- Which pokemon has the more skilled trainer

Finally, evaluate if any of my pokemon will evolve. There are only two ways that a pokemon can evolve:
- If it is a pokemon that evolves by leveling up, it must be at least the required level
- If it is a pokemon that evolves by evolution stone, it must be exposed to that stone
Be sure to check how each of my pokemon level up, and ensure that they only level up under the appropriate circumstances.
As soon as the evolution conditions for a pokemon are met, it immediately evolves. Pokemon evolution does not happen subtly or gradually, it is an impressive and spectacular process.
firstInput:
The turn begins as I wake up in <<location>>, where I am currently staying.
As I wake up, I receive a package that I have been eagerly anticipating.
It contains two items that I have been dreaming of for years - my trainer card, and a pokeball with my first pokemon.
As I turn over the trainer card in my hand, I am filled with hopes and dreams - the dream of becoming pokemon champion.
I summon my pokemon from its pokeball, eager to see it with my own eyes, giddy that I finally have a pokemon of my own.
I deliberate if I want to give it a nickname, and if so what the nickname should be.
My starting pokemon is:
<<pokemon>>

instructionBlocks.content:
Each pokemon has one or two types, and each type can be one of the following:
- Normal: Offensively strong vs none. Offensively weak vs Rock, Steel; no effect on Ghost. Defensively immune to Ghost. Defensively weak vs Fighting.
- Fire: Offensively strong vs Grass, Ice, Bug, Steel. Offensively weak vs Fire, Water, Rock, Dragon. Defensively strong vs Fire, Grass, Ice, Bug, Steel, Fairy. Defensively weak vs Water, Ground, Rock.
- Water: Offensively strong vs Fire, Ground, Rock. Offensively weak vs Water, Grass, Dragon. Defensively strong vs Fire, Water, Ice, Steel. Defensively weak vs Electric, Grass.
- Electric: Offensively strong vs Water, Flying. Offensively weak vs Electric, Grass, Dragon; no effect on Ground. Defensively strong vs Electric, Flying, Steel. Defensively weak vs Ground.
- Grass: Offensively strong vs Water, Ground, Rock. Offensively weak vs Fire, Grass, Poison, Flying, Bug, Dragon, Steel. Defensively strong vs Water, Electric, Grass, Ground. Defensively weak vs Fire, Ice, Poison, Flying, Bug.
- Ice: Offensively strong vs Grass, Ground, Flying, Dragon. Offensively weak vs Fire, Water, Ice, Steel. Defensively strong vs Ice. Defensively weak vs Fire, Fighting, Rock, Steel.
- Fighting: Offensively strong vs Normal, Ice, Rock, Dark, Steel. Offensively weak vs Poison, Flying, Psychic, Bug, Fairy; no effect on Ghost. Defensively strong vs Bug, Rock, Dark. Defensively weak vs Flying, Psychic, Fairy.
- Poison: Offensively strong vs Grass, Fairy. Offensively weak vs Poison, Ground, Rock, Ghost; no effect on Steel. Defensively strong vs Grass, Fighting, Poison, Bug, Fairy. Defensively weak vs Ground, Psychic.
- Ground: Offensively strong vs Fire, Electric, Poison, Rock, Steel. Offensively weak vs Grass, Bug; no effect on Flying. Defensively strong vs Poison, Rock; immune to Electric. Defensively weak vs Water, Grass, Ice.
- Flying: Offensively strong vs Grass, Fighting, Bug. Offensively weak vs Electric, Rock, Steel. Defensively strong vs Grass, Fighting, Bug; immune to Ground. Defensively weak vs Electric, Ice, Rock.
- Psychic: Offensively strong vs Fighting, Poison. Offensively weak vs Psychic, Steel; no effect on Dark. Defensively strong vs Fighting, Psychic. Defensively weak vs Bug, Ghost, Dark.
- Bug: Offensively strong vs Grass, Psychic, Dark. Offensively weak vs Fire, Fighting, Poison, Flying, Ghost, Steel, Fairy. Defensively strong vs Grass, Fighting, Ground. Defensively weak vs Fire, Flying, Rock.
- Rock: Offensively strong vs Fire, Ice, Flying, Bug. Offensively weak vs Fighting, Ground, Steel. Defensively strong vs Normal, Fire, Poison, Flying. Defensively weak vs Water, Grass, Fighting, Ground, Steel.
- Ghost: Offensively strong vs Psychic, Ghost. Offensively weak vs Dark; no effect on Normal. Defensively strong vs Poison, Bug; immune to Normal, Fighting. Defensively weak vs Ghost, Dark.
- Dragon: Offensively strong vs Dragon. Offensively weak vs Steel; no effect on Fairy. Defensively strong vs Fire, Water, Electric, Grass. Defensively weak vs Ice, Dragon, Fairy.
- Dark: Offensively strong vs Psychic, Ghost. Offensively weak vs Fighting, Dark, Fairy. Defensively strong vs Ghost, Dark; immune to Psychic. Defensively weak vs Fighting, Bug, Fairy.
- Steel: Offensively strong vs Ice, Rock, Fairy. Offensively weak vs Fire, Water, Electric, Steel. Defensively strong vs Normal, Grass, Ice, Flying, Psychic, Bug, Rock, Dragon, Steel, Fairy; immune to Poison. Defensively weak vs Fire, Fighting, Ground.
- Fairy: Offensively strong vs Fighting, Dragon, Dark. Offensively weak vs Fire, Poison, Steel. Defensively strong vs Fighting, Bug, Dark; immune to Dragon. Defensively weak vs Poison, Steel.

instructionBlocks.content:
Whenever I defeat a trainer, each of the pokemon in my current party level up exactly once, to a limit of <<(number_of_owned_badges*5)+20>>. Whenever I defeat a wild pokemon, each of the pokemon in my current party level up exactly once, to a limit of <<(number_of_owned_badges*5)+10>>. When a pokemon reaches an evolution threshold, it immediately evolves.

Pokemon may also evolve when exposed to evolution stones. These stones can be found in caves or in the wild, or they can be bought from large stores. If a pokemon is exposed to an appropriate evolution stone, it immediately evolves.
instructionBlocks.name: Leveling up

instructionBlocks.content:
Anybody who possesses pokemon possesses a trainer license and is considered a pokemon trainer. Any trainer may challenge another trainer to battle, and the challenged trainer may not refuse. Although some trainers may not enjoy battling, they can always be challenged and will always accept.

Each gym leader gives out badges for defeating them. When I defeat a gym leader, they will give me the badge corresponding to their gym.
instructionBlocks.name: Trainer fights

instructionBlocks.content: Although routes may involve difficult terrain, they will always be traversable. Pokemon may make travel easier (such as by surfing or rock climbing), but I will always be able to travel any route without using pokemon, by walking or swimming.
instructionBlocks.name: Travel

instructionBlocks.content: Pokemon centers are subsizied by the pokemon league and offer their services completely free of charge. Each pokemon is operated by Nurse Joy, a young pink-haired woman in a nurse outfit. Each Nurse Joy is a sister of each other, having the family name Joy. Similarly, all police officers are sisters from a very large family named Officer Jenny.
instructionBlocks.name: Pokemon centers

instructionBlocks.content: When considering if I encounter a trainer, do not make up any trainers other than the ones listed. If I am in a region with notable NPCs or pokemon encounters, make sure to feature them. If a legendary pokemon makes its lair in a location, make sure you describe how the power of that pokemon warps and shapes the environment - even approaching a legendary pokemon is a significant challenge.
instructionBlocks.name: Encounters

instructionBlocks.content:
Pokemon come in five tiers of rarity, each with increasing power and prestige:
- Common (eg Rattata, Pidgey) are commonplace and unremarkable
- Uncommon (eg Rhyhorn, Porygon) signify that the trainer has moderate experience
- Rare (eg Clefairy, Ninetales) require great skill and wealth to train
- Elite (eg Gyarados, Dragonite) can only be trained by the most skilled trainers
- Legendary (eg Zapdos, Mewtwo) are like forces of nature, unable to be tamed by humans
instructionBlocks.name: Rarities

instructionBlocks.content:
When illustrating a pokemon, you must include the name of the pokemon several times in the appearance description. For example:
`Bulbasaur: A small quadrupedal creature about two feet in length, with a blue-green body and a darker green bulb protruding from its back. Bulbasaur. The bulb has faint ridges and is covered in a wax coating. Bulbasaur.

instructions:
This is set in the world of pokemon. I am an eighteen-year-old trainer aspiring to become Champion. To do this, I will need to defeat all eight gym leaders, then the elite four and the current champion. Along the way, I will have several encounters with other trainers, including my rival.

The tone is gritty and realistic. I can fail. I can lose battles and face the consequences. NPCs have their own motivations and don't exist just to help me. The world doesn't pull punches. In pokemon battles, the trainers are at very real risk of being injured or killed.

loreBookEntries.content:
PALLET TOWN:

A tiny, sleepy coastal town at the southern tip of Kanto with only a handful of houses, dirt paths, and a gentle sea breeze carrying the scent of salt and wildflowers. The town's most notable feature is Professor Oak's Laboratory, a large building on a hill at the edge of town where the renowned pokemon researcher conducts his work and provides starter pokemon to new trainers.

There is no Pokemon Center or Poke Mart here - just homes, the lab, and the shore. A narrow strip of beach runs along the south side where the water stretches out toward Cinnabar Island. Route 1 heads north through tall grass toward Viridian City. Despite its small size, Pallet Town has produced some of the most accomplished trainers in Kanto's history.

Professor Oak has a collection of Bulbasaurs, Charmanders and Squirtles. A trainer who beats Oak in a battle may claim one of these pokemon.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- North: `Kanto Route 1`
- South: `Kanto Route 21`

NPC encounters:
- Professor Oak (Bulbasaur, Charmander, Squirtle) can be found in his laboratory.
- Delia (Mr. Mime) is Red's mother, and can be found in her house. She may be challenged to a battle.
- Daisy (Clefairy, Chansey) is Leaf's older sister, and can be found in her house. She may be challenged to a battle.
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Pallet Town

loreBookEntries.content:
VIRIDIAN CITY:

A mid-sized city sitting at the edge of the sprawling Viridian Forest, surrounded by lush greenery and well-kept gardens. The city serves as the gateway between southern Kanto and the forest routes leading north toward Pewter City, as well as the western path toward the Pokemon League via Route 22.

Viridian City has a Pokemon Center, a Poke Mart, and the Trainer School where beginners learn the basics. Its gym is run by Giovanni, the secretive Ground-type specialist. The gym's puzzle of spinning floor tiles is notoriously disorienting. Older residents speak of the city's peaceful reputation, though Team Rocket's shadow has touched even here.

Trainers:
- Black Belt Atsushi (Machop, Machoke, Machamp) is a trainer at the gym.
- Tamer Jasper (Arbok, Tauros) is a trainer at the gym.
- Cooltrainer Samuel (Sandslash, Rhyhorn, Nidorino) is a trainer at the gym.
- Cooltrainer Yuji (Sandslash, Graveler, Onix, Marowak) is a trainer at the gym.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- South: `Kanto Route 1`
- North: `Kanto Route 2`
- West: `Kanto Route 22`

NPC encounters:
- Giovanni is the gym leader, but he will refuse to battle trainers with fewer than six badges.
- Julia (Pidgey, Rattata) runs the trainer school, and serves as guide to pokemon battling. She may be challenged to a battle.
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Viridian City

loreBookEntries.content:
PEWTER CITY:

A grey, austere city built from the same stone as the mountains that loom behind it to the east. The buildings are squat and sturdy, and the streets have a quiet, serious atmosphere. Pewter City is most known for its Museum of Science, which houses rare fossil exhibits and a replica of a prehistoric pokemon skeleton that draws researchers from across the region.

The city's gym, the first official challenge for trainers coming from the south, is run by Brock - a stoic, dependable young man who specializes in Rock-type pokemon. His gym is a straightforward affair of rocky terrain and boulders. North of the city, Route 3 winds eastward through hilly trainer-packed grassland toward Mt. Moon.

Trainers:
- Camper Liam (Geodude, Sandshrew) is a trainer at the gym.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- South: `Viridian Forest`
- East: `Kanto Route 3`

NPC encounters:
- Brock is the gym leader.
- Lola (Omanyte, Kabuto) runs the Museum of Science. She may be challenged to a battle.
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Pewter City

loreBookEntries.content:
CERULEAN CITY:

A bright, clean city crisscrossed by canals and streams fed by the rivers flowing down from the mountains to the north. The water is famously clear - you can see Goldeen darting beneath the bridges. Houses are painted in cheerful blues and whites, and the whole city has an open, airy feel.

Misty, a fierce and temperamental Water-type specialist, runs the gym here - a converted swimming pool complex where challengers fight on floating platforms. North of the city, the famous Nugget Bridge crosses the river toward Route 25 and Bill's Sea Cottage. To the east, Route 9 climbs into rugged hills toward Rock Tunnel. South, Route 5 leads toward Saffron City. A mysterious cave in the hills northwest of the city is sealed off, said to contain pokemon of extraordinary power. It may only be entered by those who possess eight badges.

Trainers:
- Swimmer Luis (Horsea, Shellder) is a trainer at the gym.
- Picnicker Diana (Goldeen) is a trainer at the gym.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- West: `Kanto Route 4`
- North: `Route 24`
- South: `Kanto Route 5`
- East: `Kanto Route 9`

NPC encounters:
- Misty is the gym leader.
- Jessica (Doduo, Ponyta, Arbok) runs the bike shop. She may be challenged to a battle.
- Cindy (Oddish, Bellsprout, Metapod) runs a service producing medicines from berries. She may be challenged to a battle.
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Cerulean City

loreBookEntries.content:
VERMILION CITY:

A loud, industrious port city on Kanto's southern coast, perpetually busy with cargo ships, fishing trawlers, and the occasional luxury liner. The harbor dominates the south side of town, and the air smells of diesel and sea spray. Warehouses and dockworker bars line the waterfront, while the residential areas further north are more orderly.

The city's gym is run by Lt. Surge, a brash foreign military veteran who earned his nickname in a war where his Electric-type pokemon saved his life. His gym is rigged with electric lock puzzles that require finding hidden switches in trash cans. The Vermilion harbor is also home to the Fan Club, where pokemon enthusiasts gather to gush about their favorites. East of the city, Route 11 stretches toward Diglett's Cave.

Trainers:
- Sailor Dwayne (Pikachu) is a trainer at the gym.
- Engineer Baily (Voltorb, Magneton) is a trainer at the gym.
- Gentleman Tucker (Pikachu) is a trainer at the gym.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- North: `Kanto Route 6`
- East: `Kanto Route 11`

NPC encounters:
- Lt. Surge is the gym leader.
- Dontae (Lapras, Rapidash, Clefable) runs the pokemon fan club. He may be challenged to a battle.
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Vermilion City

loreBookEntries.content:
LAVENDER TOWN:

A small, somber town perpetually draped in a thin grey mist that rolls in from the surrounding hills. The buildings are old and weather-worn, the streets quiet except for the distant sound of wind chimes hung outside nearly every door - a local custom said to comfort the spirits of departed pokemon. The town has no gym, no game corner, nothing to draw tourists but grief.

The dominant structure is Pokemon Tower, a seven-story burial monument visible from every corner of town, where trainers come to pay respects to pokemon that have passed on. A small Pokemon Center and a volunteer-run house where Mr. Fuji tends to abandoned pokemon are the only real services. Routes lead west to Route 8 toward Saffron City and south along Route 12 down the coast.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- West: `Kanto Route 8`
- North: `Rock Tunnel`
- East: `Pokemon Tower`
- South: `Kanto Route 12`

NPC encounters:
- Evelyn (Lickitung, Fearow, Raichu) runs a small radio broadcast out of her home. She may be challenged to a battle.
- Rebecca (Arcanine, Tauros, Victreebell) runs a trainer house for trainers coming from Rock Tunnel to recover. She may be challenged to a battle.
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Lavender Town

loreBookEntries.content:
CELADON CITY:

The largest city in Kanto, sprawling and green, with wide boulevards lined with manicured trees and ornamental gardens. The air smells faintly of perfume from the city's famous fragrance shops. A massive department store dominates the skyline - six floors of everything a trainer could ever need, from evolution stones to TMs. Behind the city's polished surface, the Game Corner operates as a front for Team Rocket's underground operations, complete with a hidden basement.

Erika, a soft-spoken but formidable Grass-type specialist, runs the city's gym - a converted greenhouse thick with vines and flowering plants. The Celadon Mansion houses the game developers, and the city's restaurant and hotel district caters to travelers from across the region. Route 7 leads east toward Saffron City, while Route 16 heads west to the top of Cycling Road.

Trainers:
- Beauty Bridget (Oddish) is a trainer at the gym.
- Lass Kay (Bellsprout) is a trainer at the gym.
- Beauty Tamia (Bellsprout) is a trainer at the gym.
- Cooltrainer Mary (Bellsprout, Oddish, Weepinbell) is a trainer at the gym.

At the game corner, Porygon and Eevees may be purchased for large amounts of money, or won in battle from the game corner attendants.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- East: `Kanto Route 7`
- West: `Kanto Route 16`

NPC encounters:
- Erika is the gym leader.
- Fiona (Flareon, Jolteon, Vaporeon) runs an Eevee breeding program out of Celadon Mansions. She may be challenged to a battle.
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Celadon City

loreBookEntries.content:
SAFFRON CITY:

The sprawling commercial and administrative heart of Kanto, ringed by guard-gated entrances and dominated by the towering Silph Co. headquarters - the region's largest manufacturer of pokemon technology. The streets are crowded and fast-paced, full of office workers, businesspeople, and trainers passing through. The city sits at the crossroads of four major routes, making it the most connected hub in the region.

Sabrina, a cold and intensely powerful Psychic-type specialist, presides over the city's gym - a disorienting maze of warp tiles that scrambles challengers' sense of direction. Across the street, the Fighting Dojo offers an alternative challenge and a Hitmonlee and Hitmonchan as a prize.

Trainers:
- Black Belt Hitoshi (Hitmonchan, Hitmonlee) is a trainer at the fighting dojo.
- Black Belt Mike (Mankey, Primeape) is a trainer at the fighting dojo.
- Black Belt Hideki (Machop, Machoke) is a trainer at the fighting dojo.
- Black Belt Aaron (Primeape) is a trainer at the fighting dojo.
- Black Belt Koichi (Machoke) is a trainer at the fighting dojo.
- Psychic Cameron (Slowpoke, Slowbro) is a trainer at the gym.
- Psychic Preston (Slowpoke, Mr. Mime) is a trainer at the gym.
- Channeler Stacy (Haunter) is a trainer at the gym.
- Channeler Amanda (Gastly) is a trainer at the gym.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- North: `Kanto Route 5`
- South: `Kanto Route 6`
- West: `Kanto Route 7`
- East: `Kanto Route 8`

loreBookEntries.name: Location: Saffron City

loreBookEntries.content:
FUCHSIA CITY:

A weathered city tucked against the southern coast of Kanto, half-hidden by the dense woods and marshland that surround it. The architecture has an older, traditional feel - wooden buildings with tiled roofs, narrow streets, and a pervasive smell of damp earth and sea salt. The city's most famous attraction is the Safari Zone, a sprawling nature preserve on its northern outskirts where rare pokemon roam in protected habitats.

Koga, a ninja master and Poison-type specialist, runs the city's gym - a building filled with invisible walls that force challengers to fumble their way through to reach him. His pokemon hit hard and rely on toxic stalling tactics. South of the city, Route 19 stretches across open water toward the Seafoam Islands, while the coastal routes to the east wind back up toward Lavender Town.

Trainers:
- Juggler Kayden (Drowzee, Hypno, Kadabra) is a trainer at the gym.
- Juggler Kirk (Voltorb, Voltorb, Voltorb, Voltorb) is a trainer at the gym.
- Tamer Edgar (Arbok, Sandslash, Arbok) is a trainer at the gym.
- Tamer Phil (Sandslash, Arbok) is a trainer at the gym.

- Martina (Ninetales, Fearow, Scyther, Arcanine) is a ranger and runs the safari zone. She may be challenged to a battle.
- Janine (Golbat, Venomoth, Weezing) is the daughter of Koga and works at the Pokemon zoo. She may be challenged to a battle.
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Fuchsia City

loreBookEntries.content:
CINNABAR ISLAND:

A small volcanic island off Kanto's southwestern coast, built on black rock and ringed by choppy grey water. The dormant volcano at the island's center radiates a low, constant heat, and steam vents hiss from cracks in the ground near the shore. The town itself is compact - a Pokemon Center, a research lab, and a scattering of houses clustered around the harbor where ferries dock.

Blaine, an eccentric and fiercely intelligent Fire-type specialist, operates his gym behind a locked door - the key hidden somewhere inside the crumbling Pokemon Mansion on the island's eastern hill. That mansion, once a cutting-edge research facility, is where scientists conducted the experiments that created Mewtwo from Mew's DNA. The building is now gutted and overgrown, infested with wild pokemon, its journals scattered among the debris.

Trainers:
- Burglar Quinn (Growlithe, Vulpix) is a trainer at the gym.
- Super Nerd Erik (Vulpix, Vulpix, Ninetales) is a trainer at the gym.
- Burglar Dusty (Ponyta) is a trainer at the gym.

loreBookEntries.name: Location: Cinnabar Island

loreBookEntries.content:
KANTO INDIGO PLATEAU:

A fortress-like complex carved into the mountains at the end of Victory Road, accessible only to trainers who have collected all eight Kanto gym badges and survived the gauntlet of the cave below. The plateau sits high above the tree line, surrounded by sheer cliffs and perpetual wind. The main Challengers face four consecutive battles with no retreat - Lorelei and her Ice-types, Bruno and his Fighting-types, Agatha and her Ghost-types, and Lance and his Dragon-types - before earning the right to challenge the reigning Champion. The halls are austere and ceremonial, lined with statues of past champions. Few trainers ever make it this far, and fewer still walk out victorious.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- South: `Kanto Victory Road`

- Agatha is the third of the elite four and must be challenged third.
- Lance is the last of the elite four and must be challenged after Lorelei, Bruno and Agatha.
- <<rival_name>> is the reigning champion and must be defeated to take the title of champion.

loreBookEntries.name: Location: Kanto Indigo Plateau

loreBookEntries.content:
KANTO ROUTE 1:

A short, well-worn dirt path winding through knee-high grass between Pallet Town and Viridian City. The route is gentle and flat, bordered by low wooden fences and scattered wildflowers - the kind of trail that lulls you into thinking the world is safe. Pidgey scatter from the brush and Rattata dart between the grass stalks, making it a rite of passage for new trainers.

There are no trainers stationed here and no real hazards beyond the occasional aggressive wild pokemon. A few ledges cut into the hillside allow quick one-way drops southward back toward Pallet Town. The route is short enough to walk in under an hour, but for a trainer with their first pokemon, it feels like the start of something enormous.

Wild pokemon:
- Pidgey
- Rattata

KANTO ROUTE 2:

A long, narrow route running north from Viridian City to Pewter City, split cleanly in two by the dense canopy of Viridian Forest. The southern section is a quiet stretch of grass and low shrubs leading to the forest entrance, while the northern exit opens into rocky, sparse terrain approaching Pewter. A gatehouse on the eastern side provides access to Diglett's Cave.

The route itself is lightly trafficked - most of the challenge lies inside the forest rather than on the path. Wild Pidgey, Rattata, and the occasional Nidoran can be found in the grass patches at either end. An item-filled area behind a cuttable tree on the north side rewards trainers who return later with the right HM.

KANTO ROUTE 3:

A winding, hilly trail east of Pewter City that marks the first real gauntlet for new trainers. The path snakes through rocky terrain dotted with sparse grass and low scrub, rising and falling over uneven ground as it approaches the foothills of Mt. Moon. Bug Catchers, Lasses, and Youngsters line the route shoulder to shoulder, eager to battle anyone passing through.

The air is drier here than in the forested routes to the west, and the soil turns from dirt to gravel the further east you go. By the time the mouth of Mt. Moon comes into view - a dark opening in the mountainside - most trainers have been through half a dozen fights. A small Pokemon Center sits just outside the cave entrance, its red roof a welcome sight.

A short, downhill stretch of rocky terrain spilling out from the eastern exit of Mt. Moon toward Cerulean City. The route drops in elevation quickly, with ledges that allow only one-way passage southward - once you jump down, there is no climbing back up without going around. A small patch of wild grass hides pokemon tougher than what most trainers encountered inside the cave.

The landscape transitions from barren mountain rock to the greener, water-fed terrain around Cerulean City. A river runs along the southern edge, accessible to trainers with Surf, opening up fishing spots and water-dwelling pokemon. The distant sound of rushing water from Cerulean's canals carries on the breeze as the city comes into view.

KANTO ROUTE 5:

A gentle southward path connecting Cerulean City to Saffron City, running through suburban outskirts and overgrown fields. The route is relatively quiet, with patches of tall grass hiding common pokemon along the roadside. A daycare center sits along the western edge, where an elderly couple will raise trainers' pokemon for a fee.

The main road leads to Saffron City's northern gate, but during Team Rocket's occupation the gate is locked tight. An underground passage accessed through a small guardhouse provides a detour, connecting to Route 6 on the other side of the city. The tunnel is cramped and dimly lit, but it beats arguing with the guards.

KANTO ROUTE 6:

A well-traveled route running south from Saffron City to Vermilion City, flanked by tall grass and a slow-moving stream that meanders alongside the path. The route is flat and open, with clusters of young trainers - Bug Catchers, Picnickers, and Campers - set up along the trail looking for battles.

The stream is a decent fishing spot, drawing out Magikarp, Poliwag, and Goldeen for patient anglers. An underground path entrance on the northern end connects to Route 5, bypassing Saffron City's locked gates. As the route nears Vermilion City, the smell of the harbor drifts in - oil, salt water, and diesel - and the sounds of the port grow louder.

KANTO ROUTE 7:

A short, paved stretch of road connecting Celadon City's eastern edge to Saffron City's western gate. The route is barely more than a city block in length, squeezed between buildings and hedgerows, with just enough wild grass to harbor a handful of pokemon species. It feels more like a gap between two cities than a proper route.

A guardhouse on the eastern end marks the entrance to Saffron City - or would, if the gates were not often barred during times of trouble. An underground path entrance nearby provides an alternative connection to Route 8 and Lavender Town. Despite its small size, the route sees heavy foot traffic from trainers moving between Kanto's two largest cities.

A moderately long east-west route connecting Saffron City to Lavender Town, lined with trainers itching for a fight. The terrain is flat and grassy, transitioning from the urban sprawl near Saffron to the quieter, more somber countryside approaching Lavender. Gamblers, Super Nerds, and Lasses stake out positions along the path.

An underground path entrance on the western end connects to Route 7, providing a shortcut to Celadon City. The eastern stretch grows noticeably quieter as Lavender Town's silhouette appears on the horizon - the pointed top of Pokemon Tower rising above the low rooftops. The mood shifts palpably; even the wild pokemon seem more subdued this close to the tower.

The path is steep and uneven, winding through patches of dry grass between large rock formations. Hikers, Picnickers, and Bug Catchers crowd the route, making it a relentless series of battles for anyone trying to pass through.

The terrain is harsh and exposed, with little shade and a constant wind blowing across the hilltops. Wild Spearow and Rattata are aggressive here, and the occasional Ekans or Sandshrew suns itself on the warm rocks. The northern section is rocky and sparse, while the southern half levels out into grassland as Lavender Town draws near. Hikers and PokeManiacs patrol the path between the two landmarks.

A river runs along the route's eastern edge, and trainers with Surf can follow it upstream to reach the abandoned Power Plant - a fenced-off industrial ruin crackling with residual energy. The route serves as a critical connector between the eastern wilds and Lavender Town, and the steady hum of electricity from the plant is audible long before it comes into view.

The path is wide and well-worn, popular with trainers of all types - Youngsters, Gamblers, and Engineers from the nearby port all congregate here looking for battles. The grass is thick with Drowzee, Ekans, and Spearow.

At the route's far eastern end, a gatehouse leads to Diglett's Cave, providing a shortcut all the way back to Route 2 near Viridian City. An upper observation deck in the gatehouse offers a view east toward Route 12, but the path forward is blocked without the PokeFlute to wake the sleeping Snorlax. The route is a fisherman's paradise - anglers line every dock and jetty, casting into the dark water below. A massive Snorlax blocks the northern section of the path, requiring the PokeFlute to rouse it from its immovable slumber.

The terrain shifts between elevated boardwalks over the water and solid ground with patches of tall grass. Wild Oddish, Bellsprout, and Venonat hide in the vegetation, while the surf below harbors Tentacool and Horsea. The route eventually turns westward into Route 13, beginning the long winding path toward Fuchsia City. The salt air is constant, and the creaking of old wood underfoot accompanies every step.

The terrain is flat coastal scrubland, with the ocean visible to the south and the sound of waves ever-present. Bird Keepers, Picnickers, Beauties, and Bikers all stake out their corners of the labyrinth, making avoidance nearly impossible.

The route connects Route 12 to the north with Route 14 to the south, forming part of the long coastal corridor between Lavender Town and Fuchsia City. Wild Ditto can occasionally be found here, disguised among the more common Pidgey and Oddish. The route offers little in the way of shelter or services - just a straight shot through trainer-heavy territory. Wild Ditto, Venonat, and various Grass-types lurk in the brush. A gatehouse at the western end provides passage into Fuchsia City proper. The route is a favorite haunt of bird trainers who use the open fields for flight practice. A massive Snorlax blocks an alternate path through the tall grass to the west, immovable without the PokeFlute.

The area north of the gate has patches of wild grass hiding Rattata, Spearow, and Doduo. Bikers congregate near the entrance, revving their engines before the long coast downhill. The slope is relentless - momentum carries you forward whether you pedal or not, and the wind whips hard enough to make conversation impossible. Bikers and Cue Balls line the route, challenging anyone who rolls past.

The road surface is cracked asphalt patched over many times, and the guardrails are dented from years of wipeouts. Wild Rattata, Spearow, and Doduo wander onto the shoulder from the grass beyond the barriers. The route has a lawless feel - no Pokemon Centers, no rest stops, just a long downhill grind through hostile territory until Fuchsia City's outskirts appear at the bottom.

loreBookEntries.content:
KANTO ROUTE 18:

A short, flat stretch at the bottom of Cycling Road where the long descent from Route 16 finally levels out. The route connects the southern end of the cycling path to Fuchsia City through a gatehouse. Bird Keepers patrol the area, taking advantage of the open sky and flat terrain to train their flying pokemon.

The grass here is coarse and windblown, home to Rattata, Spearow, Fearow, and Doduo. After the relentless downhill gauntlet of Cycling Road, the route feels almost peaceful - a brief reprieve before reaching Fuchsia City's gates. The smell of the sea is strong here, carried inland from Route 19's waters just south of the city.

loreBookEntries.content:
KANTO ROUTE 19:

A wide stretch of open ocean south of Fuchsia City, accessible only by Surf. The water is deep and dark blue, choppy with currents that push southward toward the Seafoam Islands. Swimmers bob between the waves, challenging any trainer who ventures out onto the water. Tentacool are everywhere, their translucent bodies flickering just below the surface.

The route has no land to speak of - just open sea from Fuchsia's shore to the rocky outcroppings near Route 20. The current is strong enough that weaker Water-type pokemon struggle against it, and the depth drops off sharply not far from shore. Horsea, Shellder, and Staryu can be fished from the deeper sections. It is a stark reminder that Kanto's waters are not gentle.

KANTO ROUTE 20:

A long east-west water route connecting the Seafoam Islands to Cinnabar Island, cutting across some of the coldest open water in Kanto. The current near the Seafoam Islands is brutal, chilled by the icy caverns beneath the surface, and the spray carries a biting cold even on warm days. Swimmers and Bird Keepers challenge travelers along the way.

The Seafoam Islands rise from the water at the route's midpoint - twin rocky islets with cave entrances visible at the waterline. West of the islands, the water warms gradually as Cinnabar Island's volcanic heat bleeds into the sea. The contrast between the freezing eastern waters and the tepid western stretch is disorienting. Tentacool, Horsea, and Staryu are common throughout.

KANTO ROUTE 21:

A water route running north from Cinnabar Island to Pallet Town, dotted with small grassy islets that break up the open ocean. The water is calm here compared to the western sea routes, and the scattered islands provide rare patches of wild grass where land-dwelling pokemon like Tangela can be found - an oddity this far out to sea.

Fishermen anchor their boats near the islands, casting lines into the deep water between them, while Swimmers patrol the open stretches. The route is one of the more scenic in Kanto - on clear days, Pallet Town's shoreline is visible to the north, and Cinnabar's volcanic peak smolders to the south. It is a quiet, almost meditative stretch of water, far removed from the chaos of the mainland routes.

KANTO ROUTE 22:

A short, rugged route heading west from Viridian City toward the Pokemon League's badge-check gates. The terrain shifts quickly from the city's manicured outskirts to wild grassland and rocky ground, with a river cutting through the southern half accessible by Surf. Nidoran, Mankey, and Spearow roam the tall grass.

The route is deceptively quiet for its importance - it is the first step on the road to the Indigo Plateau, and a rival trainer may ambush you here early in your journey. The guard gate at the western end checks badges before allowing passage to Route 23 and Victory Road beyond. The mountains loom larger with every step west, a reminder of the challenge that awaits.

ROUTE 23:

A long, winding route stretching from the badge-check gates west of Viridian City to the entrance of Victory Road. The path passes through a series of guard stations - one for each gym badge - where officials verify a trainer's credentials before allowing them to proceed. The terrain grows increasingly harsh: open grassland gives way to rocky highlands, then to the base of the mountains.

Rivers and ponds cut across the route, requiring Surf to navigate, and the wild pokemon here are among the strongest found on any Kanto route - Primeape, Arbok, Sandslash, and Fearow all roam freely. The air thins as the elevation climbs, and the final stretch before Victory Road's cave entrance is a steep, punishing ascent. By the time you reach the cave mouth, the flatlands of Kanto are far below.

ROUTE 24:

A famous bridge spanning the river north of Cerulean City, known to every trainer in Kanto as Nugget Bridge. Five trainers stand in sequence along the bridge's length, challenging all comers, with a supposed prize of a gold nugget awaiting anyone who defeats all five - though the man at the end turns out to be a Team Rocket recruiter.

The bridge itself is a sturdy wooden structure over fast-moving water, with views of the surrounding hills and the path continuing north toward Route 25. Wild pokemon lurk in the grass on the northern bank, including Oddish, Bellsprout, and the elusive Abra. The water below can be surfed, revealing Tentacool, Horsea, and other aquatic pokemon. It is one of the most iconic early-game challenges in the region.

ROUTE 25:

A winding eastward path beyond Nugget Bridge, cutting through hilly terrain toward the isolated Sea Cottage where the pokemon researcher Bill lives and works. The route is packed with trainers - Hikers, Youngsters, Lasses, and Campers - who take advantage of the foot traffic heading to and from Bill's place. The grass is thick and the terrain uneven, with rocky outcrops breaking up the path.

Bill's Sea Cottage sits at the route's eastern terminus, perched on a cliff overlooking the ocean. The researcher is known for his work on the pokemon storage system and has a habit of getting himself into strange predicaments. Wild pokemon in the grass mirror those on Route 24, and the water along the shore hides Krabby and Horsea for trainers willing to fish.

VIRIDIAN FOREST:

A dense, shadowy forest filling the gap between Viridian City and Pewter City, its canopy so thick that sunlight barely reaches the forest floor. The paths twist and branch in confusing patterns through walls of ancient trees, fallen logs, and tangled undergrowth. Bug-type pokemon are everywhere - Caterpie and Weedle dangle from branches, Kakuna and Metapod hang motionless from tree trunks, and the rare Pikachu darts through the underbrush.

Novice Bug Catchers patrol the trails, nets in hand, eager to test their newly caught teams against any passing trainer. The forest is disorienting for first-timers, though the paths do eventually lead through to the other side. The air is cool and damp, thick with the smell of rotting leaves and moss. It is a rite of passage for any trainer heading north to Pewter City - simple in hindsight, but unsettling on a first trip through.

MT. MOON:

A sprawling, multi-level cave system bored through the mountain between Pewter City and Cerulean City. The interior is pitch dark in places, lit only by the faint phosphorescent glow of mineral deposits and the occasional shaft of light from cracks in the ceiling. Zubat swarm in dense clouds, Geodude cling to the walls, and Paras scuttle through the damp lower chambers. Rare Clefairy are said to dance here under the light of the full moon.

The cave is infamous for Team Rocket activity - grunts and scientists have been spotted excavating rare fossils from the deeper tunnels. Moon Stones, fallen meteorite fragments with evolutionary properties, can be found embedded in the cave walls. The tunnels are confusing and full of dead ends, and the constant dripping of water and echo of footsteps make it difficult to tell how deep you have gone.

The valuable fossils can be sold for money to shady buyers on the black market, or brought to Cinnabar Island to be resurrected into Kabuto, Omanyte or Aerodactyl.

DIGLETT'S CAVE:

A long, straight underground tunnel running beneath the surface between Route 2 near Viridian City and Route 11 east of Vermilion City. The tunnel is remarkably clean and well-bored, carved entirely by the Diglett and Dugtrio that inhabit it - the walls are smooth packed earth, and the floor is soft dirt. The air is cool and carries a faint mineral smell.

The tunnel is a vital shortcut connecting the western and eastern halves of southern Kanto, saving hours of travel through multiple cities. The Diglett here are territorial but not especially dangerous, though the occasional Dugtrio can catch an unprepared trainer off guard with its speed and power. There are no other trainers inside - just you, the dark, and the constant sound of something burrowing just out of sight.

ROCK TUNNEL:

A pitch-black underground passage connecting Route 9 to Route 10, threading through the mountains east of Cerulean City. Without Flash, the cave is navigated entirely by feel - trainers stumble through invisible walls, trip over ledges, and blunder into wild pokemon and other trainers in the dark. Even with Flash, the tunnels are cramped, winding, and claustrophobic.

The cave is home to Zubat, Geodude, Machop, and Onix, all of which are aggressive in the confined spaces. Hikers, PokeManiacs, and Picnickers who have set up camp inside challenge anyone who crosses their path. The tunnel spans two floors, with ladders connecting the levels, and the air grows colder and damper the deeper you go. Emerging into the daylight on Route 10 feels like surfacing from deep water.

POKEMON TOWER:

A seven-story tower in the heart of Lavender Town serving as a burial ground and memorial for deceased pokemon. The lower floors are lined with headstones and memorial plaques, while the upper floors grow increasingly decrepit - cracked tiles, flickering lights, and the pervasive smell of old incense. Ghost-type pokemon haunt every level, and the Channelers who tend the graves have been driven mad by the spirits, attacking anyone who enters.

An unidentifiable ghost blocks the stairway to the upper floors, impossible to fight or flee from without the Silph Scope to reveal its true form. Team Rocket grunts occupy the top floor, having disturbed the rest of a Marowak whose spirit now roams the tower in anguish. Mr. Fuji, Lavender Town's beloved elder, has been taken hostage at the summit. The tower is deeply unsettling - the air is cold, the walls seem to breathe, and the wailing never fully stops.

SAFARI ZONE:

A vast, walled nature preserve on the outskirts of Fuchsia City, divided into four distinct zones of varying terrain - open grassland, marshland, rocky hills, and dense forest. Trainers pay an entry fee and receive thirty Safari Balls and limited time to explore. Standard battling is forbidden inside; instead, trainers must rely on bait and rocks to lure or startle wild pokemon before throwing a ball.

The Safari Zone is home to pokemon found nowhere else in Kanto - Kangaskhan, Tauros, Scyther, Pinsir, and the incredibly rare Chansey all roam the tall grass. Deep in the preserve, a hidden house rewards trainers who navigate the maze-like terrain with the HM for Surf. Dratini can be fished from the ponds in the innermost areas. The whole place feels wild and unmanaged despite its boundaries, as if the preserve has been slowly reclaimed by the pokemon inside it.

SEAFOAM ISLANDS:

The interior is a labyrinth of frozen floors, underground rivers, and massive boulders that must be pushed into the current to dam the water flow and create navigable paths. The air inside is frigid, and ice coats every surface - walls, floors, even the pokemon that live here.

Seel, Dewgong, Shellder, and Psyduck inhabit the frozen chambers, and the deepest level is said to be the resting place of Articuno, the legendary bird of ice. The caverns are difficult to navigate, due to the combination of water currents, boulders and biting cold.Few trainers brave the cold long enough to reach the bottom.

POKEMON MANSION:

A gutted, crumbling mansion on Cinnabar Island that once housed a state-of-the-art pokemon research laboratory. The building is three stories of collapsed floors, shattered windows, and fire-scorched walls, with a basement level accessible through holes in the weakened structure. Wild Koffing, Grimer, Ponyta, and Growlithe have infested every corner, and the whole place reeks of chemical residue and decay.

Scattered journal entries found on desks and laboratory tables tell the story of the Mewtwo project - how scientists discovered Mew in the wild, brought it here, and engineered a vastly more powerful clone that eventually broke free and destroyed the facility. Dittos are the remains of failed attempts to clone Mew.. The key to Blaine's gym is hidden in the upper levels, forcing trainers to pick through the wreckage. Burglar and Scientist trainers still prowl the halls, scavenging what is left.

POWER PLANT:

An abandoned industrial power station on the river east of Cerulean City, accessible only by surfing downstream from Route 10. The building is a hulking concrete structure surrounded by rusted chain-link fencing and warning signs that no one heeds. Inside, the machinery still hums with residual electricity, and the air crackles with static - your hair stands on end the moment you step through the door.

The plant is overrun with Electric-type pokemon drawn to the ambient energy: Voltorb and Electrode litter the floor disguised as item balls, Magnemite cluster around old generators, and Electabuzz stalk the deeper corridors. At the heart of the facility, the legendary Zapdos roosts among the sparking transformers. The flickering lights and constant electrical buzz make the place feel alive in a way that is deeply unsettling for a building that has been officially decommissioned for years.

KANTO VICTORY ROAD:

A brutal, multi-level cave system carved into the mountains between Route 23 and the Indigo Plateau. The tunnels are dark, winding, and full of dead ends. Massive boulders block paths and must be pushed into position using Strength, while sheer cliff faces require Rock Climb. The pokemon here are among the strongest wild encounters in Kanto - Machoke, Marowak, and Graveler lurk in every shadow.

Only trainers who have earned all eight badges and passed every checkpoint on Route 23 are permitted entry. The Cooltrainers who train inside Victory Road are elite - many have attempted the League challenge before and failed. The cave is deliberately grueling, a final filter to ensure only the truly prepared reach the Indigo Plateau beyond.

loreBookEntries.content:
CERULEAN CAVE:

A massive, labyrinthine cave system in the hills northwest of Cerulean City, sealed off by vast and echoing, with underground rivers, crystalline rock formations, and multiple levels connected by ladders and water passages. The wild pokemon inside are extraordinarily powerful - Golbat, Kadabra, Electrode, and Chansey at levels that would overwhelm most trainers.

The cave's deepest chamber, accessible only by surfing across an underground lake, is the dwelling place of Mewtwo - the engineered pokemon that escaped from the Cinnabar Island research facility and retreated here. The cave pulses with psychic energy; trainers report headaches, disorientation, and the unsettling feeling of being watched from the moment they enter. It is the most dangerous location in Kanto, and it exists for one purpose: to test the very best.

Wild pokemon:
- Golbat
- Graveler
- Parasect
- Psyduck
- Golduck
- Kadabra
- Geodude
- Machoke
- Magneton
- Dodrio
- Electrode
- Chansey
- Ditto
- Wobbuffet
- Larvitar
- Lickitung
- Magikarp
- Gyarados
- Slowpoke
- Slowbro
- Horsea
- Krabby

In the deepest corner of Cerulean cave is the legendary pokemon, Mewtwo. Paused in deep meditation, it psychically observes and tracks all humans and pokemon in Cerulean cave, using its powerful telekinesis to impede anyone who would try to approach it. The psychic energy distorts the cave and disorients anyone who would try to approach Mewtwo.

- East: `Route 24`

loreBookEntries.name: Location: Cerulean Cave

loreBookEntries.content:
NEW BARK TOWN:

A tiny, wind-swept town perched on the eastern edge of Johto where the land meets the sea. The constant breeze that rolls in off the water gives the place its name - locals say the winds here carry the promise of new beginnings. There is little to the town beyond a cluster of modest homes, a few weather-beaten docks, and the prominent research laboratory of Professor Elm, a brilliant but absent-minded pokemon scientist who studies breeding and evolution patterns.

The town has no Pokemon Center, no Poke Mart, and no gym - just the quiet rhythm of a coastal settlement where everyone knows everyone. Route 29 heads west through rolling grassland toward Cherrygrove City, and the waters to the south and east are deep enough to surf, though cold currents and Tentacool make casual swimming inadvisable. Despite its isolation, New Bark Town has sent more than a few trainers out into the world who went on to make a name for themselves.

Professor Elm has a collection of Chikoritas, Cyndaquils and Totodiles. A trainer who beats Elm in a battle may claim one of these pokemon.

Professor Elm occasionally has Togepi eggs available for promising trainers.

Rachel (Drowzee, Exeggcute) is Ethan's mother and can be found in her house. She may be challenged to a battle.

Melissa (Krabby, Oddish, Kakuna) is Lyra's mother and can be found in her house. She may be challenged to a battle.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- West: `Route 29`
- East: `Johto Victory Road`
loreBookEntries.name: Location: New Bark Town

loreBookEntries.content:
CHERRYGROVE CITY:

A quaint coastal city sitting where the hills of western Johto ease down into the sea, its streets lined with flowering trees that bloom in vivid pink and white for most of the year. The sweet fragrance is unmistakable - travelers coming down Route 29 smell Cherrygrove before they see it. The city is small and unhurried, with a Pokemon Center, a modest Poke Mart, and a handful of homes clustered near the waterfront.

An elderly man who lives near the city entrance takes it upon himself to give guided tours to new trainers passing through, pointing out the landmarks with genuine pride. The shore to the south is rocky but fishable, and the waters are populated by Tentacool, Krabby, and Corsola. Route 30 heads north toward Violet City, making Cherrygrove the natural first rest stop for anyone setting out from New Bark Town. It is a gentle place - the calm before the real journey begins.

Gemma (Noctowl, Shellder) offers tours of the city to promote tourism. She may be challenged to a battle.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- East: `Route 29`
- North: `Route 30`
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Cherrygrove City

loreBookEntries.content:
VIOLET CITY:

A city steeped in history and tradition, built on elevated ground in central Johto where the terrain begins to rise toward the mountains. The architecture is distinctly old-fashioned, with tiled rooftops and wooden buildings that speak to centuries of continuous habitation. The skyline is dominated by Sprout Tower, a towering wooden pagoda that sways visibly in the wind, and the streets are quieter than most cities, with an atmosphere more scholarly than commercial.

Falkner, the city's gym leader, is a proud and somewhat intense young man who inherited the position from his father. He specializes in Flying-type pokemon and runs his gym from an elevated platform that forces challengers to fight with the wind at their backs - or in their faces. Sprout Tower, just north of the gym, serves as an informal proving ground where monks train alongside their Bellsprout and test the character of trainers before they challenge Falkner. Route 32 heads south along the coast toward Union Cave, while Route 36 connects westward toward the heart of Johto.

Trainers:
- Bird Keeper Abe (Spearow)
- Bird Keeper Rod (Pidgey, Pidgey)

Paula (Chansey, Bellsprout, Geodude) runs the trainer school. She may be challenged to a battle.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- East: `Route 31`
- North: `Sprout Tower`
- South: `Route 32`
- West: `Route 36`
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Violet City

loreBookEntries.content:
AZALEA TOWN:

A small, rustic town tucked into the edge of a dense forest in southern Johto, where the air is thick with humidity and the sound of insects never fully fades. The buildings are simple wooden structures, many with mossy roofs, and the whole place feels like it is slowly being reclaimed by the surrounding woodland. The town has a deep connection to Slowpoke - the locals revere the dopey creatures as sacred, believing their yawns bring the rain. Slowpoke wander freely through the streets, lounging on porches and blocking doorways without a care.

Bugsy, the town's gym leader, is a young prodigy obsessed with Bug-type pokemon to an almost academic degree. Despite his youth, his knowledge of bug behavior and battle strategy is formidable, and his Scyther has humbled more than a few overconfident challengers. Kurt, an elderly craftsman who lives at the north end of town, is one of the last people in Johto who can fashion pokeballs by hand from Apricorns - a dying art that trainers travel far to take advantage of. The entrance to Slowpoke Well sits at the town's edge, and Ilex Forest looms to the west.

Trainers:
- Bug Catcher Benny (Weedle, Kakuna, Beedrill)
- Twins Amy & May (Spinarak, Ledyba)
- Bug Catcher Al (Caterpie, Weedle)

Anna (Growlithe, Ponyta, Magmar) runs the charcoal kiln. She may be challenged to a battle.

Brittany (Scyther, Pinsir, Heracross) is a specialist pokeball artisan. She may be challenged to a battle.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- East: `Route 33`
- North: `Slowpoke Well`
- West: `Ilex Forest`
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Azalea Town

loreBookEntries.content:
GOLDENROD CITY:

Johto's largest and most boisterous city, a sprawling commercial hub that pulses with energy at all hours. The streets are wide and packed with people - shoppers, businessmen, trainers, street performers, and the occasional shady character hawking questionable goods in back alleys. The Goldenrod Department Store, the largest in the region, towers over the central district and sells everything from evolutionary stones to rare TMs. The Radio Tower, an iconic spire visible from nearly anywhere in the city, broadcasts music, talk shows, and trainer tips across all of Johto.

Whitney, the city's gym leader, is a cheerful and deceptively sweet young woman whose Normal-type pokemon - particularly her infamous Miltank - have reduced countless challengers to frustrated tears. Her gym is a maze of Clefairy-themed decorations that belies the brutal efficiency of her battle strategy. The city also houses the Global Terminal, the Goldenrod Game Corner, the Magnet Train station connecting to Saffron City in Kanto, and an underground tunnel lined with shops. Route 35 heads north toward the National Park, while Route 34 runs south through the Day Care toward Ilex Forest.

Trainers:
- Lass Carrie (Snubbull)
- Beauty Samantha (Meowth, Meowth)
- Lass Bridget (Jigglypuff, Jigglypuff, Jigglypuff)

At the game corner, Porygon and Eevees may be purchased for large amounts of money, or won in battle from the game corner attendants.

Ruby (Doduo, Furret) runs the bike shop. She may be challenged to a battle.

Lily (Dunsparce, Flaaffy) runs a pokemon grooming and name rating service. She may be challenged to a battle.

Samantha (Jumpluff, Goldeen) is a radio personality working at the radio station. She may be challenged to a battle.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- South: `Route 34`
- North: `Route 35`
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Goldenrod City

loreBookEntries.content:
ECRUTEAK CITY:

An ancient city of wooden temples, pagodas, and autumn-colored trees that feels like stepping back several hundred years. The streets are paved with worn stone, and paper lanterns hang from the eaves of buildings that have stood for generations. Ecruteak is the spiritual heart of Johto - a place where the old legends of Ho-Oh and the three beasts are not folklore but living tradition. Two towers define the city: the Bell Tower to the northeast, a pristine multi-story pagoda where Ho-Oh is said to return, and the Burned Tower to the northwest, a charred ruin where lightning struck centuries ago and three unnamed pokemon perished, only to be resurrected by Ho-Oh's sacred flames.

Morty, the city's gym leader, is a contemplative and somewhat enigmatic young man who specializes in Ghost-type pokemon. He claims to have the ability to see the future and has devoted his life to encountering Ho-Oh - a goal that borders on obsession. His gym is shrouded in darkness, with an invisible floor path over a void that challengers must navigate by memory. The Kimono Girls, a troupe of traditional dancers who each carry an evolved form of Eevee, perform at the dance theater in the city's center. Routes 38 and 42 branch west and east respectively, while Route 37 connects southward.

Trainers:
- Sage Ping (Gastly, Gastly, Gastly, Gastly, Gastly)
- Medium Martha (Gastly, Haunter)
- Medium Grace (Haunter)
- Sage Jeffrey (Haunter)

The kimono girls are five young female trainers, each of which has a different evolution of Eevee. They may be challenged to a battle, rewarding the victor with an Eevee.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- South: `Route 37`
- North: `Burned Tower`
- North: `Bell Tower`
- West: `Route 38`
- East: `Route 42`
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Ecruteak City

loreBookEntries.content:
OLIVINE CITY:

A busy port city on Johto's western coast where the smell of brine and engine oil hangs permanently in the air. The harbor is the city's lifeblood - cargo ships and ferries come and go daily, connecting Johto to distant regions and the isolated Cianwood City across the bay. The Olivine Lighthouse, a tall beacon on the southern bluff, guides ships through the treacherous coastal waters, though its light has been known to falter when its resident Ampharos, affectionately named Amphy, falls ill.

Jasmine, the city's gym leader, is a shy and gentle young woman whose quiet demeanor belies her skill with Steel-type pokemon. She was once a Rock-type specialist before discovering her affinity for Steel, and her Steelix is a formidable opponent that has ended many challenger runs. Jasmine is deeply compassionate - she personally tends to the sick Ampharos in the lighthouse and has been known to delay gym battles to care for injured pokemon. The city connects to Route 38 heading east toward Ecruteak, and Routes 40 and 41 stretch across the open water to the south and southwest.

Trainers:
- Gentleman Preston (Growlithe)
- Lass Connie (Marill)

Jasmine, the Gym Leader of Olivine, often spends time in the city lighthouse, tending to its resident Ampharos, Amphy.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- North: `Route 39`
- West: `Route 40`
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Olivine City

loreBookEntries.content:
CIANWOOD CITY:

A remote, weather-beaten city clinging to the rocky shore of a peninsula across the sea from Olivine, reachable only by surfing through the rough waters of Routes 40 and 41. The isolation has given Cianwood a rugged independence - the buildings are squat and built to withstand ocean storms, and the locals are hardened by a life lived far from Johto's commercial centers. The city is famous for its pharmacy, which produces a rare and potent medicine called the SecretPotion, unavailable anywhere else in the region.

Chuck, the city's gym leader, is a loud, barrel-chested man who trains as hard as his Fighting-type pokemon. He meditates under the waterfall behind his gym and is known to challenge visitors to physical contests before agreeing to battle. His gym sits directly beneath a cascading waterfall, and the sound of rushing water makes it difficult to hear commands - a deliberate design that forces trainers and pokemon to rely on instinct and trust. Route 47, a rugged coastal path added to maps in recent years, leads west toward the Cliff Cave and the Safari Zone.

Trainers:
- Black Belt Yoshi (Hitmonlee)
- Black Belt Lao (Hitmonchan)
- Black Belt Nob (Machop, Machoke)

Carmine (Shuckle, Sandshrew) runs a photography studio. She may be challenged to a battle.

Erin (Chansey) runs a pharmacy that produces specialized medicine for pokemon. She may be challenged to a battle.

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- East: `Route 41`
- West: `Cliff Cave`
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Cianwood City

loreBookEntries.content:
MAHOGANY TOWN:

A small, quiet mountain town nestled in a valley between the Lake of Rage to the north and the Ice Path to the east, surrounded by dense pine forests that darken early in the winter months. The air here is noticeably colder than the rest of Johto, and frost clings to the rooftops well into spring. On the surface, Mahogany Town appears unremarkable - a few homes, a Pokemon Center, and a nondescript souvenir shop that sells oddly overpriced Ragecandybars. Beneath that shop, however, Team Rocket once operated a hidden base that broadcast a signal forcing Magikarp in the Lake of Rage to evolve prematurely.

Pryce, the city's gym leader, is an elderly man whose icy composure matches his specialty. A former trainer of legendary skill in his youth, Pryce suffered a personal loss decades ago involving a Piloswine that left him emotionally withdrawn. His gym is a frozen arena where the floor is slicked with ice, forcing challengers to slide helplessly unless they solve the movement puzzle. Despite his cold exterior, those who earn his badge speak of a quiet warmth in his eyes. Route 43 leads north to the Lake of Rage, while Route 44 heads east toward the treacherous Ice Path.

Trainers:
- Boarder Ronald (Seel, Dewgong)
- Skier Roxanne (Jynx)
- Boarder Brad (Swinub, Swinub)
- Skier Clarissa (Dewgong)

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- West: `Route 42`
- North: `Route 43`
- East: `Route 44`
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Mahogany Town

loreBookEntries.content:
BLACKTHORN CITY:

A remote, imposing city carved into the mountains of northeastern Johto, accessible only through the Ice Path from the west or the steep descent of Route 45 to the south. The buildings are built from dark stone quarried from the surrounding peaks, and the streets are narrow and steep, winding between cliffs. The city has a severe beauty to it - sharp mountain air, dramatic views of the valleys below, and a perpetual sense of being at the edge of civilization. Behind the city lies the Dragon's Den, a sacred cavern and lake where Dragon-type masters have trained for centuries.

Clair, the city's gym leader, is a fierce, proud woman from a long lineage of Dragon tamers - she is the cousin of Lance, the Pokemon League Champion. She specializes in Dragon-type pokemon and has a reputation for refusing to hand over badges to trainers she deems unworthy, even after they have defeated her, insisting they prove themselves further in the Dragon's Den. Her gym is a lava-floored arena that requires navigating moving platforms over molten rock. Clair's Kingdra, her signature pokemon, has ended more championship dreams than perhaps any other gym leader's ace in the region.

Trainers:
- Cooltrainer Fran (Seadra)
- Cooltrainer Cody (Horsea, Seadra)
- Cooltrainer Mike (Dragonair)
- Cooltrainer Lola (Dratini, Dragonair)

From this location, I can travel to the following locations:
- North: `Ice Path`
- West: `Dragon's Den`
- South: `Route 45`
- East: `Mt. Silver`
loreBookEntries.name: Location: Blackthorn City

loreBookEntries.content:
ROUTE 29:

A gentle, well-worn path cutting through low rolling hills and tall grass between New Bark Town and Cherrygrove City. The route is short and straightforward - a dirt trail flanked by wildflowers and the occasional fruit tree, with the sound of Pidgey calls drifting down from the canopy. For most trainers setting out from New Bark Town, this is their first taste of the wild, and the pokemon here are appropriately mild-mannered.

The terrain is flat and forgiving, with clear sightlines in every direction and no real hazards to speak of. A small path branches north toward Route 46, offering a tantalizing glimpse of the mountainous terrain that awaits more experienced trainers. Sentret stand upright on their tails along the roadside, watching travelers pass with wary curiosity. By night, Hoothoot take over the patrol, their steady hooting a constant backdrop for anyone camping along the way.

Wild pokemon:
- Pidgey
- Sentret
- Rattata
- Hoothoot

Aipom may be encountered here, but they are rare encounters, and highly sought after by trainers.

Murkrow may be encountered here, but they are rare encounters, and highly sought after by trainers.

- West: `Cherrygrove City`

loreBookEntries.content:
ROUTE 30:

A narrow northward trail climbing gently from Cherrygrove City through patches of forest and open meadow. Berry trees line the path at regular intervals, their branches heavy with fruit that trainers and pokemon alike help themselves to. The route splits partway through - the main path continues north toward Route 31 and Violet City, while a side trail leads to a modest house on a hill where Mr. Pokemon, an eccentric collector of rare finds, entertains visitors with tea and excited rambling about his latest discoveries.

The grass is thicker here than on Route 29, and the bug pokemon are more active - Caterpie and Weedle hang from low branches, and Ledyba cluster on tree trunks in the early morning. Youngster Joey, a local trainer of modest skill but unshakable confidence, patrols the lower section of the route and will eagerly challenge anyone who makes eye contact. The path narrows as it approaches the northern end, where the tree cover thickens and the terrain begins to rise toward Violet City.

- Caterpie
- Metapod
- Weedle
- Kakuna
- Ledyba

- Poliwag

loreBookEntries.name: Location: Route 30

loreBookEntries.content:
ROUTE 31:

A short, transitional route connecting the northern end of Route 30 to the western gates of Violet City. The path runs through mixed terrain - patches of tall grass give way to rocky outcroppings where the foothills begin to assert themselves. The most notable feature is a dark opening in the hillside on the route's southern edge: the entrance to Dark Cave, a sprawling underground system that extends deep beneath the mountains.

Bellsprout appear in the grass here for the first time, their thin stems swaying as they track passersby. A small pond near the route's midpoint attracts Poliwag and the occasional fisherman. The sounds of Violet City - distant bells, the creak of Sprout Tower - become audible as travelers approach the eastern end. A guardhouse marks the transition from wilderness to civilization, staffed by an attendant who offers directions to the gym and tower.

- Caterpie
- Metapod
- Weedle
- Kakuna
- Ledyba

- West: `Violet City`

loreBookEntries.name: Location: Route 31

loreBookEntries.content:
ROUTE 32:

A long, scenic route running south from Violet City along the Johto coastline, eventually terminating at the entrance to Union Cave. The path is a mix of dirt trail and wooden boardwalk, with the sea visible to the east for most of the journey. The elevated overpass of the Magnet Train line crosses overhead about midway down, its steel framework casting long shadows in the afternoon sun. Mareep graze in the grassy sections, their wool crackling with static on dry days, while Wooper splash in the tidal pools near the shore.

The route is long enough that most trainers need to rest at least once along the way, and the density of trainers - fishermen along the coast, youngsters and campers on the inland path - makes it a gauntlet for anyone trying to rush through. The Ruins of Alph lie just to the west, accessible through a side path that branches off near the midpoint. As the route nears its southern end, the terrain becomes rockier and the air cooler, signaling the approach of Union Cave's gaping entrance.

- Mareep
- Hoppip
- Zubat

loreBookEntries.content:
ROUTE 33:

A short, perpetually damp stretch of trail connecting the western exit of Union Cave to Azalea Town. Rain falls here more often than not - the local geography creates a microclimate where moisture rolling in from the south gets trapped against the mountainside, resulting in near-constant drizzle. The path is muddy and slippery, flanked by mossy boulders and stunted trees that lean away from the prevailing wind.

Despite its brevity, the route has a miserable reputation among trainers. The ground is uneven, visibility is poor in heavy rain, and the wild pokemon - Geodude, Rattata, and the occasional Hoppip caught in an updraft - tend to be agitated by the weather. A lone Hiker named Anthony stations himself along the path, seemingly unbothered by the perpetual wetness. The lights of Azalea Town glimmer through the rain at the route's western end, a welcome sight for anyone emerging from the damp darkness of Union Cave.

Wild pokemon:
- Rattata
- Spearow
- Ekans
- Geodude
- Zubat
- Hoppip

loreBookEntries.content:
ROUTE 34:

A pleasant, well-maintained route running south from Goldenrod City through open grassland to the northern edge of Ilex Forest. The terrain is flat and easy, with neatly trimmed hedgerows lining parts of the path and a gentle stream running parallel to the road. The route's most prominent feature is the Pokemon Day Care, a sprawling ranch run by an elderly couple who will raise trainers' pokemon for a fee - and occasionally discover an egg left behind by their charges.

The mix of wild pokemon here is unusually diverse, with Abra teleporting away at the first sign of trouble, Drowzee lurking in the tall grass, and the extremely rare Ditto hiding in plain sight. An Officer patrols the southern section near the forest entrance, keeping the route safe for younger trainers. The coastal section to the east is accessible via Surf, opening up fishing spots where Krabby, Corsola, and Staryu can be found. Goldenrod's skyline is visible to the north, a constant reminder of civilization's proximity.

- Cleffa
- Abra
- Elekid
- Ditto

- Staryu

loreBookEntries.name: Location: Route 34

loreBookEntries.content:
ROUTE 35:

A northward route leading from Goldenrod City's upper gate toward the National Park, passing through grassland dotted with wildflowers and buzzing with insect activity. The terrain is gently rolling, with scattered trees providing shade for the trainers who congregate here in surprising numbers - Bug Catchers, Campers, Picnickers, Jugglers, and even the occasional Officer keeping the peace.

The diversity of wild pokemon is notable: Nidoran of both genders forage in the underbrush, Yanma dart between clearings with audible wingbeats, and Drowzee shuffle through the tall grass with vacant expressions. A stream runs along the route's western edge where Psyduck and Poliwag can be found. The route culminates at the grand gates of the National Park, a manicured green space visible over the treetops well before you arrive. The atmosphere shifts noticeably as you move north - Goldenrod's urban noise fades, replaced by birdsong and rustling leaves.

Wild pokemon:
- Pidgey
- Nidoran-F
- Nidoran-M
- Drowzee
- Ditto
- Yanma
- Abra
- Psyduck

- Poliwhirl
